tools.description: List the terminal sessions linked to this agent: name, id, working directory, shell state (ready/running), and the most recent command. Linked terminals are the only ones reachable.
tools.name: list_terminals

tools.description: Type a command into a linked terminal's live shell and wait for it to finish; returns its output and exit code. The shell's state (cwd, env, modules, remote ssh) applies and persists. If a command is already running, this queues until the prompt returns (bounded by queue_timeout_ms).

command.description: Single-line shell command (join steps with ';' or '&&')

queue_timeout_ms.description: Max wait for the shell's prompt before typing (default 15000, cap 600000; 0 = only if free now)

terminal.description: Linked terminal: session id or display name (as in @term:NAME)

timeout_ms.description: Max runtime once typed (default 30000, cap 3600000). On timeout the command keeps running and partial output is returned.

tools.name: run_in_terminal

tools.description: Read a linked terminal's recent activity: the command journal (commands, outputs, exit codes) by default, or the visible screen text with screen=true (for TUIs, boot output, or shells without integration marks).

commands.description: How many recent journal entries (default 5, cap 50)

screen.description: Return the visible screen text instead of the journal

terminal.description: Linked terminal: session id or display name

tools.name: read_terminal

tools.description: The full guide to writing documents the user reads in Chimaera: the portable markdown dialect (it also renders on GitHub and in Obsidian), links and embeds with fragments, frontmatter, and how to reference files in replies. Read it before writing a report, README or notes.
tools.name: document_guide

tools.description: Check a markdown document before handing it over: broken relative links and embeds, missing heading anchors and line ranges, dangling footnotes, absolute local paths, images without alt text or over 10 MB, and syntax GitHub shows as literal text (wikilinks, MDX, ::: blocks, MyST directives, unsupported alert types). Returns each issue with its line and a fix.

path.description: The markdown file: relative to this session's working directory (then the workspace root), or absolute

tools.name: check_document

tools.description: Show the user a Chimaera desktop notification (it reaches them even when Chimaera is in the background). Use it when the user asked to be told about something ("ping me when the build is done", "let me know if the job fails"), or when long-running work you were watching finishes or fails mid-turn. The user is already notified automatically when your turn ends or you need permission/input, so do not use it for routine progress. Rate-limited per session.

message.description: The notification text: one or two short sentences with the outcome.

title.description: Optional short headline (defaults to this session's name).

tools.name: notify

tools.description: Show the user a web app you started (a dev server, a notebook, a dashboard) in a Chimaera browser pane beside this session. Only addresses on this host, loopback, or a node of the user's running Slurm jobs open; for anything else, give the user the URL. A successful call says nothing about whether the page loaded or works. Once open, the pane is shared with you: the browser_* tools read and drive it with the user watching (browser_navigate to the same app reuses it). To check something without touching the user's view, use a hidden page (browser_navigate to another app, or page "own"). Call once per app, not on every reload. Rate-limited per session.

url.description: The app's http:// address, e.g. http://localhost:5173/ (path and query are kept; a port is required unless the host is loopback).

tools.name: open_browser

tools.description: Open a web app and wait for it to load (up to 15 s). Checking something opens a hidden page of your own; a pane the user is watching (one you opened with open_browser, say) is reused only for the same app, navigated in place. Page "own" always means the hidden page (to check something in the background without touching the user's view); page "p1" sends a shared pane to another app. Only addresses on this host, loopback, or a node of the user's running Slurm jobs load. Your own page is invisible to the user until you call browser_show. `url` may also be "back", "forward" or "reload". Returns the final URL, title and HTTP status when known. The app engine loads pages through Chimaera's proxy, so an app that calls absolute /api/v1 or /ws/ paths (Chimaera's own UI) reaches the hosting daemon instead of itself: start that page with engine "chromium".

engine.description: The engine for a NEW own page (default: app when a Chimaera app window is connected, else chromium). A page never changes engine: close yours with browser_close first.

height.description: Viewport height in CSS px for your own page (default 800).

page.description: "own" (your hidden page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: the shared pane showing the same app, else your hidden page.

url.description: An http:// address, e.g. http://localhost:8888/lab, or back/forward/reload.

width.description: Viewport width in CSS px for your own page (default 1280).

tools.name: browser_navigate

tools.description: The page as compact text: roles, names and states, each interactive element tagged with a ref ([e12] button "Run") that browser_click, browser_type and the other tools take. The cheap default way to see a page.

max_chars.description: Cap on the text (default 24000, at most 100000).

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

viewport_only.description: Only what is scrolled into view (landmarks kept).

tools.name: browser_snapshot

tools.description: An image of the viewport, the full page, or one element (by ref or CSS selector): PNG (JPEG when large), at most 1600 px wide and 2000 px on its long edge. A page too tall to stay legible in one image gives the viewport instead.

full_page.description: The whole scrollable page (capped in height).

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

ref.description: An element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. "e12".

selector.description: A CSS selector for the element to capture.

tools.name: browser_screenshot

tools.description: One element by ref or CSS selector: outerHTML (first 4 KB), attributes, computed styles (a default set, or the properties named), its box, and whether it is visible or covered.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

ref.description: An element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. "e12".

styles.description: CSS property names to report instead of the default set.

tools.name: browser_inspect

tools.description: The page's live DOM serialized now, or with original=true the original response body (fetched again by the page). Paged: pass the returned next offset.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

tools.name: browser_source

tools.description: Click an element by ref (scrolled into view first) or at x,y in CSS px, with real mouse input. A native <select> is refused: use browser_select. Returns what changed, and the URL and title after.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the action.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

ref.description: An element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. "e12".

tools.name: browser_click

tools.description: Type text with real keyboard input into the focused element, or into `ref` after clicking it. submit=true presses Enter after. per_key=true sends one key event per character (slower; for pages that listen to keydown) instead of inserting the text.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

ref.description: An element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. "e12".

tools.name: browser_type

tools.description: Press one key with real keyboard input: Enter, Tab, Escape, Backspace, Delete, ArrowUp/Down/Left/Right, Home, End, PageUp, PageDown, Space, Insert, or a single character (with modifiers for shortcuts, e.g. key "a" + ["meta"]).

modifiers.description: Modifier keys held during the action.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

tools.name: browser_press

tools.description: Scroll with the mouse wheel by dy (and dx) CSS px, over `ref` (a scrollable element) or the middle of the viewport. Positive dy scrolls down.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

ref.description: An element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. "e12".

tools.name: browser_scroll

tools.description: Choose an option of a native <select> (by ref) by its value or its visible label; fires input and change like a person's choice.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

ref.description: An element ref from browser_snapshot, e.g. "e12".

tools.name: browser_select

tools.description: Console messages and uncaught errors since your last call on this page.

level.description: error: errors and uncaught exceptions; warn: those and warnings; all (default).

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

tools.name: browser_console

tools.description: Failed (HTTP status >= 400, network error) and slow (>= 1 s) requests since your last call on this page. No bodies.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

tools.name: browser_network

tools.description: Wait until the page shows `text`, an element matches `selector`, and/or the network is idle (nothing in flight for 500 ms); all given conditions must hold. Answers ok or timeout.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

tools.name: browser_wait

tools.description: Run JavaScript in the page: `script` is an async function body; what it returns comes back as JSON (first 20 KB). On the app engine it runs in an isolated world (the page's DOM, not its JavaScript globals); on Chromium in the page's own world.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

tools.name: browser_eval

tools.description: Hand your own page to the user: it opens as a browser pane beside you. On the app engine it is the same live page (nothing reloads) and becomes a shared pane you can keep using; on Chromium the pane loads the same URL afresh in the user's window.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

tools.name: browser_show

tools.description: Close your own page (it is also closed after 10 idle minutes). Panes the user shared stay theirs.

page.description: "own" (your own page) or a shared pane's id ("p1"…). Default: your own page when you have one; otherwise the pane the user shared with you, if exactly one is.

tools.name: browser_close

tools.description: List every page you can see: your hidden page, panes shared with you (pN, you can drive them) and panes the user has open in this workspace (vN, read-only: the read tools work on them with page "vN"; ask the user to share one to act).
tools.name: browser_pages
